name: Jaddua
title: High Priest after the Exile
summary: Jaddua was a high priest in Jerusalem during the period following the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned in the book of Nehemiah as the last high priest recorded in the Old Testament, marking the end of the biblical priestly line. According to tradition, he served at a time when Persian rule gave way to Greek governance under Alexander the Great.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the priestly genealogy
keyEvents.description: Jaddua is mentioned as part of the Levitical priesthood that was recorded during Nehemiah's time, representing an important part of Israel's spiritual continuity after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Recorded as head of the priestly line
keyEvents.description: Jaddua is listed among the heads of the Levites who were recorded in the chronicle during the reign of the Persian king Darius.

keyEvents.title: Part of the high priestly lineage
keyEvents.description: Jaddua is mentioned as the son of Jonathan (also called Johanan) in the high priestly lineage that extends from Joshua, son of Jehozadak, through Joiakim, Eliashib, and Joiada.

keyEvents.title: Registration of the Levites
keyEvents.description: The heads of the Levite families were recorded in the book of Chronicles up to the time of Jaddua as high priest, marking the final period of the biblical historical archive.

keyEvents.title: Last mentioned high priest in the Old Testament
keyEvents.description: Jaddua represents the last high priest named in the canonical scriptures and marks the transition to the intertestamental period in Israel's history.
